name: calendar.created first-seen: the earliest sighting of a duplicate counts, measured from the unit start
notes: §4.1 (v1.3): a calendar.created candidate needs observedAt ≥ start(p,t) − beforeClaimMin, comparing the earliest observedAt of all observations sharing its contentHash; duplicates count once, keeping the lowest id, then the earliest observedAt.

Subject-only calendar claims: applicable timeProximity 2500, subjectOverlap 1500; Σw = 4000; window targetAt ± 3 days. The grant binds gcal.event to acct-a; three passes (acct-a, all calendars) saw [10-01, 11-01], synced 09:00, 14:00:15 and 14:40.

c1 'Q3 review' targetAt 10-08 14:00, claimed 14:02. o1 and o2 are the same event row (same content, no row key → same contentHash, same id: assertIds), seen at 09:00 (o1) and again at 14:40 (o2). The group's earliest observedAt is 09:00 < start(14:02) − 2 min = 14:00 → the event was already on the calendar → not a candidate. Window ⊆ coverage → full; graceElapsed (14:40 ≥ end(14:03) + 30) → not_found, FINAL, no account_unbound (bound). Checking the later sighting alone (14:40 ≥ 14:00) would give VERIFIED 1/1.

c2 'Budget sync' targetAt 10-14 10:00, claimed 14:02:30 (minute precision: unit [14:02:00, 14:03:00]) × o3 'Budget sync' at 10-14 10:00, first seen 14:00:15. Bound: start(p,t) − 2 min = 14:00:00 ≤ 14:00:15 → a candidate. tp 1 (Δ 0), subject 1 → 1/1 → verified, FINAL (14:40 ≥ end(14:03) + 30). Measuring from the raw claimedAt (14:00:30) would reject o3 → not_found.
o1/o2 (10-08) lie outside c2's window [10-11 10:00, 10-17 10:00] and o3 (10-14) outside c1's [10-05 14:00, 10-11 14:00]. The duplicate is an orphan with no activity → no receipt.
